title: Legible text
rationale: The single most commercially decisive image capability and the one that moves most between releases. A model that cannot set six words correctly cannot make an ad, a thumbnail, or a menu.
prompt:
A hand-painted sandwich board outside a coffee shop. The board reads exactly:
CLOSED MONDAYS
OPEN 7-4 OTHERWISE
Chalk on black, slightly uneven letterforms, wet pavement, early morning.

variants.prompt:
A pink neon sign on a dark brick wall inside a bar. The sign reads exactly:
LAST ORDERS
11:45 PM
Glass tubes and their mounts visible, a soft glow on the bricks, no other text in frame.

A close-up of a crumpled paper receipt on a café table. The printed lines read exactly:
FLAT WHITE 3.40
CROISSANT 2.85
TOTAL 6.25
Thermal print in a monospaced face, a coffee ring on the paper.

A screen-printed concert poster pasted on a wall. Top line in large letters, exactly: CAFÉ SOCIÉTÉ. Below it, smaller, exactly: Jeudi 14 mars · 20h30. Two inks, orange and navy, slightly misregistered, one corner torn.

A product shot of a matte white tub of hand cream on a beige surface. The label reads exactly:
OAT & SHEA
HAND CREAM
75 ml
Centred sans-serif label, soft studio light.

A yellow sticky note on a laptop screen. Handwritten in black marker it says exactly:
call Jo back
before 3pm!!
Shallow depth of field, the screen behind it blurred.

A blue enamel street sign on a pale stone wall, photographed from slightly below. It reads exactly: Rue des Quatre-Vents. A smaller line under it reads exactly: 6e Arr. Every accent and hyphen correct, no other text in frame.

A café chalkboard menu on a wall, photographed straight on. It reads exactly, one item per line:
SOUP OF THE DAY 6
GRILLED CHEESE 8
KALE SALAD 9
BROWNIE 4
No extra items, prices aligned on the right.

rubric: Is every character of the requested copy correct?
Is the line break where the prompt put it?
Does the lettering sit on the surface with correct perspective?
Craft of the surrounding image, once text is judged
